scope: Daily source-anchored screening of all active editorial lines. Nonpublic editorial audit only; does not establish negative evidence across every possible source or perform public-system reconciliation.

reviewed_lines.note: MT-GM-2026-10-24 staged ready:true; 23 Oct cross-region flash PMI, US Treasury yields, UK retail, Michigan sentiment, IBGE IPCA-15; no public approval implied.
LSEG Lipper 21 Oct US fund flows show large-cap subscriptions and small-cap redemptions; covered within today's macro. A one-week fund sample does not establish new global wealth/control stocks.

23 Oct UK HM Treasury announced tariff-suspension extension and proposed administrative savings; a structural discovery candidate is reserved for Atlas, not a demonstrated countrywide productivity outcome.
UK institutional policy proposal and French business disruption were screened; neither alone supports a full updated country dossier with independently verified multi-year mechanisms.
World Bank 20 Oct digital strategy and shared GPU initiative are strategy announcements, not measured deployment at scale or replicated engineering breakthrough.
World Bank digital strategy and UK regulatory process checked; no verified new technical capability, performance replication or industrial scale to justify monthly assessment.

S&P Global 23 Oct eurozone survey attributes some French disruption to unrest; energy-market threats remain attributed reports. No new independently verified battlefield or physical throughput change for standalone conflict system.
UK Treasury, ECB, World Bank and corporate PMI actors reviewed; no evidence of new control over strategic assets or a transfer of ownership justifying a separate actor report.
US Treasury 23 Oct nominal curve and 23 Oct flash PMIs covered in Global Macro; no separate newly effective monetary settlement rule verified.
UK 23 Oct announced tariff-suspension extension, filing simplification and consultation; proposal and future effective dates kept separate from operational results, tracked in Atlas.
UK administrative saving estimates (£800m annual total) are government projections, not measured ex-post outcomes; no policy-effect study yet.
S&P Global October investment-manager survey is expressed preference, not proprietary capital allocation or evidence of a new market architecture.
US fund flow compilation and sovereign par yields do not provide a new audited global wealth ownership or control census.
No new comparable annual cross-country wealth/control balance sheet established by the screened 23 Oct releases.
World Bank 20 Oct digital strategy and UK 23 Oct regulatory proposals screened; neither is a new binding global institution.
UK tariff-suspension extension concerns domestic import duties, not proof of a newly operating bilateral/regional trade agreement; Pix–TIPS remains feasibility-stage from prior scan.
World Bank 20 Oct digital access strategy raises access/skills/AI questions, but no measured societal outcome or scaled deployment change for a separate essay.

FAO October food-price surveillance and UK tariff suspensions including food/drinks screened; no newly measured food availability, nutrition or pesticide exposure shock sufficient for standalone analysis.

WOAH October animal vaccine prioritisation and antimicrobial resistance agenda considered; expert prioritisation is not measured reduced antimicrobial use, and no new herd management efficacy result verified.
Middle East energy-route risks and European civil unrest screened conditionally; threats and claims not promoted to verified imminent war or physical supply loss.

WHO DRC Ebola situation and previous pandemic research reviewed at screening level; no new independently verified 23 Oct outbreak acceleration, vaccine efficacy or biosecurity governance change suitable for another article.

selection_rationale: Today's cross-region flash PMI evidence is used in mandatory Global Macro. UK 23 Oct administrative/tariff announcement has a plausible structural mechanism but is not yet an implemented, outcome-measured policy, so it is Atlas discovery rather than a duplicate thematic article.
